title: Resolve subtoken boundary and chat-template mismatches during model onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: During recent model onboarding runs we observed several onboarding failures and subtle regressions caused by tokenizer/chat-template incompatibilities. Symptoms include: template truncation that drops assistant system tokens, unexpected subtoken splits that change token counts used for performance profiling, and misaligned prompt->kv-cache offsets that trigger decoding errors in the serving runtime.

Why this matters: Performance profiles and version pinning both depend on accurate token counts and template fidelity. If onboarding uses the wrong tokenizer or a mismatched chat template encoding, the published performance profile (tokens/sec, peak memory, latency at N tokens) will be inaccurate. That leads to bad model selection and routing decisions, billing surprises for customers, and potential runtime errors for on-prem/Dedicated deployments.

This ticket centralizes fixes and tooling to assure tokenizer and chat-template compatibility during onboarding and performance profile publishing so profiles and pinned versions are reproducible for serving runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Onboarding pipeline detects tokenizer encoding (BPE/byte-level/wordpiece) and fails fast when a chat-template cannot be encoded losslessly; 2) Template validator emits actionable warnings and auto-normalizes common mismatches (NFKC, invisible whitespace) with an audit trail; 3) Performance profiles are generated using the exact tokenizer binary and model weights that will be pinned in the catalog; 4) End-to-end test where sample prompts produce identical token counts in onboarding, published profile runner, and serving runtime; 5) New tests added to CI and a rollout runbook available.
technical_approach:
1) Add a TokenizerCompatibility step to the onboarding pipeline. This step will: detect tokenizer kind/version (via model metadata or tokenizer.json heuristics), run a canonical set of templates and prompt samples through the tokenizer, and record subtoken boundaries and boundary anomalies.

2) Implement a Template Encoder/Validator library in onboarding (python) that: applies normalization (NFKC by default), checks for invisible control chars, verifies round-trip decoding where applicable, and computes a canonical token map for templates. The validator returns either OK, Transformable (with suggested transform), or Incompatible.

3) Tie performance profile generator to the pinned tokenizer: when we publish a performance profile, we store tokenizer checksum and tokenizer version string in the profile metadata. The profile runner will re-run the microbenchmarks with that tokenizer to produce tokens/sec and latency numbers.

4) Add a small shim in the serving runtime that verifies the model catalog's tokenizer checksum before accepting requests for that model on private/Dedicated (opt-in) — this is a non-blocking safety check that logs mismatches to the console and observability pipeline.

5) Backwards-compat: for older models without tokenizer metadata, use heuristic detection and a compatibility-score threshold. If below threshold, mark onboarding as Requires Manual Review.

6) Add integration tests: (a) onnx/gpt-style model with known weird tokenization (e.g., underscores and emoji edge cases); (b) open-model that previously caused template truncation.

Estimated changes live across onboarding service, catalog publishing code, and a few SDK validators. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/218, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4521 (runtime checksum log).
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for Template Encoder/Validator covering NFKC, control chars, and round-trip tokenization.
- Integration test: onboarding -> publish profile -> runtime validation with sample prompts; verify token counts and latency buckets match within 3%.
- Load test: run performance profile generation on a 1k-sample workload to validate stability of tokens/sec numbers.
- Manual verification: QA runs model A/B where A is pinned with new flow and B is old onboarding; compare production-like request outcomes on staging.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable TokenizerCompatibility step for all new onboarding jobs; block publish if Incompatible and notify SE. Phase 2 (pilot): opt a subset of existing models to re-run profile generation and republish with tokenizer checksum. Phase 3 (gradual): make validator warnings surface in Console and add an opt-in runtime checksum check for Dedicated. Communicate to customers through release notes and provide a migration runbook for private deployments.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Heuristic tokenizer detection may misidentify edge-case tokenizers -> Mitigation: conservative thresholds and manual review + opt-out.
Risk: Normalization (NFKC) might alter customer prompts -> Mitigation: only auto-normalize templates, not user-provided dynamic prompts; show diff in audit trail.
Risk: Extra onboarding time for full profile re-run -> Mitigation: run profiles at lower sample counts initially and schedule full re-profiling during off-peak windows.
